CDF Derivatives of a Location-Scale Family

Source: R/cdf_derivatives.R
loc_scale_cdf_deriv.Rd

Closed-form derivatives of \(F\) for a family that is location-scale in its first two parameters.

Usage

loc_scale_cdf_deriv(distrib, q, theta, order)

Arguments

distrib

An object inheriting from class "distrib".

q

A numeric vector of quantiles.

theta

A named list of parameters, location first and scale second.

order

The derivative order, 1 or 2.

Value

A named list of derivative component vectors of \(F\).

Details

With \(z = (q - \mu)/\sigma\) and \(\ell_y = \partial \log f/\partial y\), $$\partial F/\partial \mu = -f, \qquad \partial F/\partial \sigma = -z f$$ $$\partial^2 F/\partial \mu^2 = f \ell_y, \qquad \partial^2 F/\partial \mu \partial \sigma = f (z \ell_y + 1/\sigma), \qquad \partial^2 F/\partial \sigma^2 = f (z^2 \ell_y + 2z/\sigma).$$

A family therefore only has to declare that it is location-scale; nothing is needed beyond its density and its response derivative, both of which every distribution already provides. This covers the censored-regression workhorses – Gaussian, logistic, Cauchy, Laplace.

See also

loc_scale_grad_cdf, loc_scale_hess_cdf
